result.summary: Introduces a BlockTemplateManager class to consolidate mining and block submission state and helpers, replacing free functions across the node layer. Adds a MempoolUpdated validation interface notification to asynchronously track fee-rate diagram chunk changes. Uses this tracked fee inflow in waitNext to determine whether a template has become stale without assembling full block templates on every tick.
result.problem: To decide whether mempool fee inflow warrants generating a new template, waitNext repeatedly locks cs_main and constructs a full block template solely to check if fee revenue increased past a threshold. Additionally, mining helper functions and template waiting utilities are scattered as free functions requiring callers to thread ChainstateManager and KernelNotifications, while SubmitBlock allocates a throwaway validation interface subscriber on each call.
evidence: PR description: 'Currently, to decide whether mempool fee inflow rose enough to be worth a new template, waitNext locks cs_main and assembles a full block template every tick just to sum its fees and compare.'
PR description: 'The fuzz test already caught a bug in the miner where it skips legitimate transactions due to an incorrect block chunk size limit check #35580.'
result.scope_notes: Large pull request (+2664/-587) spanning txmempool, validation interface signals, mining, and RPC; approximately half the diff consists of new unit tests and a new fuzz harness (src/test/fuzz/block_template_manager.cpp). It builds directly on the BlockTemplateManager refactoring introduced in PR 35675.
result.card: Introduces BlockTemplateManager to coordinate block template creation and submission, and tracks mempool fee inflow asynchronously through validation interface chunk notifications. Currently, waitNext repeatedly acquires cs_main and constructs full block templates every tick solely to determine if fee increases justify a new template. By tracking fee-rate diagram deltas across mempool updates, waitNext can detect staleness without redundant block assembly. This change is based on PR 35675.
